judgement.itemRank: Proposed, not yet confirmed by review.
judgement.minAge: No age floors on any item. See decision 7 -- the absence is reasoned, not skipped.
judgement.durations: Empty exceptions is deliberate: every item carries all six bands, including long-time.
judgement.feelsFeverish: Item 1 must carry the shared fact `feels-feverish`. It takes that fact from l-007/l-008, s-020, c-023, e-019 and t-019, which are NOT to be deleted -- the dedupe is by fact, so the region-anchored wordings remain the fallback.
judgement.semanticCautionNotEnforceable: Decision 1's 'never invert item 10 in the question' (cough must be asked present-positive) is a semantic constraint, not a phrase, and screen.mjs cannot enforce it. Recorded so its absence is not read as an oversight.

bannedPhrases: sepsis|septic|meningit|meningococc|kawasaki|pneumonia|bronchiolit|urine infection|\bUTI\b|bladder infection|kidney infection|bacteraemia|bacteremia|blood poisoning|encephalit|osteomyelit|malaria|measles|influenza|\bflu\b|covid|\bPIMS\b|leukaemia|leukemia|cancer
names a diagnosis to the child
fever|febrile|temperature|degrees|thermometer|antipyretic
item 1 asks about a sensation, never a measurement; 'have you got a temperature' is British for fever
\brigor|\brigors\b
clinical term -- a child says shaking
\bpoorly\b
British for ill; a US child reads it as an adverb
off colour|off color
British for unwell, and colour is an excluded observer criterion (item 28)
\bsick\b
UK English 'sick' means vomiting, US English means becoming ill -- unresolvable on a child's screen; say 'throw up'
\bwee\b|\bwees\b|\bweeing\b|\bwee-wee\b
British; the register is 'pee'
\bnappy\b|\bnappies\b
British, and infant-only in any case
\bunwell\b
British-leaning clinical register, and it is the vague global judgement item 29 excludes
blanch|\bglass\b|tumbler|does it fade|go(es)? away when you (push|press)|push on the (rash|spots)|press on the (rash|spots)
the blanching test is performed by an adult on a child, never delegated to the patient (item 33)
\bpinch\b|press on|feel your pulse|count your breath|in a mirror|how fast are you breathing
asks the child to examine or measure themselves (items 26, 27, 28, 32)
\bfit\b|\bfits\b|seizure|convulsion|black(ed)? out|\bfaint
a child who has had a seizure cannot report it -- that is what a seizure is (item 31)
how (ill|sick|unwell)|do you look|look sick|are you very
asks the child for the clinician's (item 29) or carer's (item 30) judgement
ethnic|\bbackground\b|country of birth|travel(led)?|where do you live|who do you live with
not the child's to report; items 37 and 39, and see 'The high-risk branch'
medicine|medication|\btablet|paracetamol|ibuprofen|tylenol|calpol|motrin
RCH: response to antipyretics does not predict severity, and it invites a child to report a dose nobody recorded (item 35)
\baccident\b|big (boy|girl)|supposed to|still dry
shaming register around bedwetting, if item 15 is ever revived
